universalPK.note: Vendor-wide NAMING CONVENTION (not one fixed field name) confirmed across dozens of objects in the HelpPage field tables: ContactKey, CommunityKey, EventKey, DiscussionKey, DiscussionPostKey, CommentKey, AnswerKey, QuestionKey, DemographicKey, AnnouncementKey, IdeationKey, VolunteerOpportunityKey, DocumentKey, LibraryKey, DocumentAttachmentKey, TenantKey, EventTypeKey, EventSessionKey, etc. -- each object's PK is a globally-unique-identifier ('guid') typed field literally named '<ObjectSingularName>Key'. Several objects ALSO carry an optional STRING-typed 'Legacy<ObjectSingularName>Key' sibling bridging to the customer's source AMS/CRM-native identifier (LegacyContactKey, LegacyGroupKey, LegacyActivityKey); several operations accept EITHER key interchangeably (Contacts/GetContact, Communities/GetContactCommunities). Runtime D4's SoftPKClassifier should treat the '<ObjectName>Key' guid field as the PK candidate, with its 'Legacy<ObjectName>Key' sibling (when present) as a unique-but-secondary alternate identifier, not a second PK. This is a PATTERN hint, not a literal fixed fieldName -- per-object PK naming still varies (e.g. ContactKey vs CommunityKey) and the exact per-IOF IsPrimaryKey flag is the extractor's job.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: Confirmed wire-level shape (Tier 2, HelpPage 'Authentication' controller, independently re-parsed by this agent's own script -- see CODE_EVIDENCE verify-integration-config-facts.mjs): POST api/v2.0/Authentication/Login accepts a LoginCredentials body {Username, Password} and returns an AuthToken {Token} (the vendor's own field description calls it an 'Encrypted Authentication String'). Step 1 trades credentials for a token; step 2 presents that token on subsequent calls -- a 'two-step' login-for-token flow, NOT OAuth2 (no client_id/redirect/scope machinery appears on this operation). The vendor's own product terminology for this credential pair is 'IAM Key' + 'IAM Password' per the operator-supplied contextHLT.md (Tier 3) -- NOT independently confirmed by Login's own generic 'Username'/'Password' field LABELS, but 'IAMKey' IS an independently HelpPage-confirmed (Tier 2) vendor term: POST Authentication/Widget's TenantInfo response model has a literal 'IAMKey' (guid) field, corroborating IAM Key as genuine Higher Logic vocabulary (surfaced on the end-user Widget-auth operation, not Login itself). This agent found NO operation-level HelpPage statement that Login's 'Username' field literally equals a tenant's 'IAM Key' value -- that specific UI-label-to-JSON-field mapping is asserted only by contextHLT.md (cross-checked elsewhere as accurate against the live HelpPage per SOURCE_STUDY.md's 'Cross-check verdict' table) and by the build brief's own framing; recorded as PROBABLE, not Tier-1/2-proven. The code-builder should confirm the exact mapping against a real tenant's credential-setup screen before shipping.

EndUserSSOMechanisms.note: SAML / OIDC SSO / OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow are END-USER community LOGIN routes (a person authenticating into the Community website/app via an external Identity Provider) -- confirmed DISTINCT from server-to-server API auth by support.higherlogic.com's 'OAuth 2.0 Code Flow' article (Tier 2, HTTP 200-verified): an authorize/token/userinfo exchange against an external IdP that resolves a 'legacy identifier' claim to log a user into the Community, with no relationship to the Community API v2.0's Login/Token mechanism or its object model. This connector's server-to-server auth is EXCLUSIVELY the Authentication/Login -> Token flow (or its unconfirmed OIDC-API-auth / legacy-v2.0 alternatives above). SSO must never be conflated with connector credential setup -- a connector build should never implement a SAML/OIDC assertion-consumer or an authorization-code redirect flow as its OWN auth path.

RoutingConvention.style: RPC-verb-in-path (ASP.NET Web API 2 auto-doc routing), NOT canonical REST resource routing
RoutingConvention.pattern: /api/v2.0/{Controller}/{OperationName}?{queryParams} for GET; a JSON request body for POST/PUT/DELETE
RoutingConvention.implication: There is no single canonical collection-root endpoint per object (no generic 'GET /api/v2.0/Contacts' that lists all contacts). Each list/get/write capability is its OWN uniquely-named RPC operation under its controller, and a given business object can have MULTIPLE candidate list operations returning overlapping or differently-shaped data (e.g. Contacts: GetMyContacts vs GetMyContactsPage vs SearchContacts vs GetContactsByDemographic). An IO's APIPath must be the SPECIFIC list operation chosen as that leaf's primary read path -- see PaginationByObject below for the one SOURCE_STUDY.md selected per leaf -- never a guessed generic collection root.
RoutingConvention.evidence: Exhaustive enumeration of all 236 operations across 25 controllers (scripts/enumerate-helppage.mjs, Tier 2); zero operations follow a bare '{Controller}/{id}' REST-collection pattern -- every operation carries an explicit verb-shaped operation name (Get*, Search*, Post*, Update*, Delete*, etc.).

IncrementalSyncCapability.note: No single vendor-wide incremental/watermark parameter exists across the Community API v2.0's 34 in-scope leaves. Confirmed real incremental mechanisms: (1) EventRegistrants -- GET Events/GetEventRegistrants (and GetRegistrantsByCalendarEvent) document a `modifiedDateTime` query parameter: a REAL, HelpPage-confirmed watermark field that filters registrants updated since a given datetime. (2) CommunityMembers -- a DEDICATED delta-window endpoint, POST System/GetCommunityMemberUpdates, accepts StartDate/EndDate and returns only contacts added-to/removed-from a community within that window (ContactCommunityUpdate model, nested CommunityAddition/CommunityRemoval) -- a delta-window mechanism, not a single 'since X' cursor field, but genuinely incremental. (3) ResourceLibraryDocuments -- GetLibraryDocuments's DaysBack parameter (default 30) is a ROLLING WINDOW ('documents from the last N days'), NOT a strict watermark -- it re-derives 'now minus N days' on every call rather than accepting an arbitrary since-timestamp; usable for incremental sync only if the sync cadence tracks its own last-run time and always chooses DaysBack >= elapsed-days-since-last-run to avoid gaps. All other 31 in-scope leaves have NO incremental filter parameter documented anywhere in the HelpPage catalog -- a full Cursor/None walk (per PaginationByObject) is the only documented mechanism for them.

Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: No vendor-documented naming/prefix convention for customer-defined custom OBJECTS was found. Higher Logic Thrive Community's extensibility surface (per this Tier-2 source) is expressed through first-class, dedicated object families -- Demographics (DemographicType/DemographicChoice, tenant-admin-configurable) and AutomationRules (tenant-configured rule schedules + a configurable fieldList) -- not through a dynamically-named custom-object family analogous to HubSpot's p_<accountID>_<name>.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: No vendor-documented naming/prefix convention for customer-defined custom FIELDS on an existing object was found. The actual per-tenant custom-field extension points are (1) Demographics -- Demographics/GetDemographicTypes + GetDemographicChoices enumerate the CURRENT tenant's configured custom demographic categories/choices attached to Contact, which a community admin can add/remove at any time (Demographics/AddDemographicCategory, AddDemographicChoice confirm these are admin-mutable) -- these are exposed as their OWN first-class DemographicType/DemographicChoice/ContactDemographic records, not as dynamically-named suffix/prefix fields on Contact's schema; and (2) AutomationRules -- GetContactDataFields (`AvailableFields`) is itself a field-catalog/schema-introspection response for a rule's configured Contact-data export, and GetContactData's own `fieldList` parameter is tenant/rule-configured. Both extension points MUST flow through runtime discovery + the framework's custom-column capture (see DiscoveryIsAuthoritative below), not a static naming-pattern marker.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No ETag, If-Match / If-Unmodified-Since header, or a version/revision field is documented on any Create/Update/Delete operation across the 236-operation catalog (confirmed by inspecting every write op's URI+body parameter tables). Objects carry plain 'UpdatedOn'/'ModifiedOn'-style timestamp fields (informational provenance, not a concurrency-control mechanism -- no operation requires or accepts a matching version/etag value on write). Conflict resolution for any future bidirectional EntityMap must use snapshot-3-way only -- do not recommend MostRecent.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsDetail: The general pattern across write-capable leaves (Blogs/DeleteBlog, Question/Delete, Answer/Delete, ResourceLibrary/DeleteLibraryDocument, ResourceLibrary/DeleteDocumentAttachment, Volunteer/WithdrawFromOpportunity*, ExternalActivity/Delete) is a plain success response ('Resource Description: None', typically 204 No Content) with NO soft-delete/archive flag or tombstone field documented on the corresponding model anywhere in this source -- treated as HARD delete per the honest-absence rule. ONE DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION: DELETE Discussions/RemovePost states verbatim 'Deletes the specified discussion post. If a message has replies, the body will be updated to: "This post was removed" and the message will be anonymized to preserve the thread structure. All documents attached to the message will be deleted.' -- i.e. DiscussionPosts is CONDITIONALLY soft-tombstoned (body replaced + author anonymized) when the post has replies, and (implicitly) hard-deleted otherwise. This is a per-object exception the code-builder MUST encode on the DiscussionPosts IO specifically -- do not generalize it to other leaves, and do not treat the vendor-wide default as soft.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Read-only default for every object per connector-code-conventions.md safety discipline, regardless of the substantial documented write surface on ~11 of 34 objects. Bidirectional sync requires sandbox validation first -- see BidirectionalPreconditions below.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: ConcurrencyControl=none (no ETag/If-Match/version field documented anywhere in the 236-operation catalog) rules out MostRecent as a safe default -- MostRecent requires a reliable revision/timestamp-of-write signal to arbitrate conflicts, which the Community API v2.0 does not expose on any write operation. DestWins is the conservative default if/when any write-capable object (DiscussionPosts, Comments/BlogComments, Questions, Answers, ResourceLibraryDocuments, Ideas, Volunteers, ExternalActivity, Blogs) is ever enabled for bidirectional sync -- it overwrites the MJ destination with the vendor's source-of-truth on pull, avoiding silent conflict-loss in either direction until a real concurrency signal is discovered.

Confirm whether the OIDC-API-auth alternative genuinely exists as a real machine-to-machine credential path -- currently a Tier-3-only, HelpPage-unconfirmed claim.

Confirm real request/response shapes for each write-capable leaf (DiscussionPosts, Comments/BlogComments, Blogs, Questions, Answers, ResourceLibraryDocuments, Ideas, Volunteers, ExternalActivity) against a live/sandbox tenant -- currently known only from HelpPage-documented sample JSON, never from a live round-trip.

Confirm the DiscussionPosts conditional soft-tombstone-vs-hard-delete behavior (RemovePost) against real production data BEFORE enabling delete-based sync on that object -- getting this wrong risks anonymizing/rewriting a real community member's post content.
Confirm no concurrency signal was missed on a live tenant (currently none documented anywhere) before ever recommending MostRecent conflict resolution.

Configuration.OutOfScopeObjectFamiliesRationale: All 6 families are genuine record/operation types the HelpPage PROVES exist (not fabricated) but were judged out of scope for an AMS/CRM sync connector -- see SOURCE_STUDY.md section 4/5 for full per-family evidence (Push API v2 confirmed via support.higherlogic.com 'Higher Logic Push API v2' article, Tier 2; ExternalSearch self-corroborated by the HelpPage's own ExternalSearch controller description text; SSO confirmed via the 'OAuth 2.0 Code Flow' support article, Tier 2; Messaging/Friends/Federation are HelpPage-proven controllers excluded by scope judgment, not by missing evidence).
Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeRationale: Set to FALSE (the conservative/safe default). There is NO complete-gamut 'describe my full schema' endpoint anywhere in the 236-operation catalog. GET System/GetApiDetails enumerates CONTROLLERS+OPERATIONS (the RPC surface itself -- Name/Endpoints/Parameters), NOT a data-object field schema, and it is not scoped to what a given IAM credential can access -- it appears to be a static reflection of the whole deployed API regardless of caller identity/entitlements (no evidence it varies per-credential). Two genuinely per-tenant, credential-gated extension points exist and MUST flow through runtime discovery + the framework's custom-column capture rather than being frozen as static metadata: (1) Demographics -- GetDemographicTypes/GetDemographicChoices enumerate the CURRENT tenant's configured custom demographic fields/categories, which differ per community and are admin-mutable at any time (AddDemographicCategory/AddDemographicChoice confirm mutability); (2) AutomationRules -- GetContactDataFields ('AvailableFields') is itself a field-catalog/schema-introspection response for a given automation rule's configured Contact-data export, and GetContactData's own 'fieldList' parameter is tenant/rule-configured, not a fixed vendor set. Because neither of these -- nor any other object -- has a describe endpoint proven to return the COMPLETE gamut a credential can access, DiscoveryIsAuthoritative stays at its conservative default; absence-on-a-later-refresh must NOT be treated as authoritative proof of removal for this connector.
